optional_context.comorbidity: post-operative day 3 hip fracture repair, chronic indwelling urinary catheter

reference_targets_freetext.item: Capillary refill time (>3 s), skin mottling over the knees, cool extremities
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Prolonged capillary refill and mottling identify hypoperfusion and track resuscitation response

reference_targets_freetext.item: Source examination: suprapubic tenderness and Costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness with catheter inspection, surgical wound, Focal crackles, skin and pressure areas, IV and line sites
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Catheter-associated urinary infection, wound infection, and pneumonia are the likely septic sources post-operatively; indispensable in febrile shock with no literature-backed substitute

reference_targets_freetext.item: Mental status and respiratory rate at the bedside (qSOFA elements)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Altered mentation and tachypnea with hypotension complete the qSOFA and mark organ dysfunction

reference_targets_freetext.item: Passive leg raise with blood pressure/pulse pressure response to gauge fluid responsiveness
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Functional bedside test that predicts response to a fluid bolus

reference_targets_freetext.item: Medication review (MAR): antihypertensives, opioids, or sedatives given in the last 6 h
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Medication effect is a common contributor to hypotension on the surgical floor

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about calf pain, unilateral leg swelling, or pleuritic chest pain; examine calves for Calf circumference asymmetry >3 cm
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Post-operative pulmonary embolism can present as fever, hypotension, and confusion

off_bedside_acceptable: cumulative fluid balance and urine output
should_not_recommend: Deferring the perfusion and source examination until lactate and cultures result
Sedating the patient for agitation before mental status and perfusion are assessed
